implementation_notes: java.time gives the date type (LocalDate is an immutable ISO-8601 calendar date, comparable, without time or zone) but no range type; ThreeTen-Extra - the proving ground that fed java.time - adds LocalDateRange, constructible from either a half-open or a closed pair, storing the start inclusive and the end exclusive, with contains(), overlaps(), abuts(), isConnected(), intersection(), union() and span(). Effectivity then means: the dated fact holds a LocalDateRange and exposes isEffectiveOn(asOf) => effective.contains(asOf). Adjacent periods abut instead of overlapping, which is exactly the semantics a non-overlap rule wants; the JDK-only variant stays available when no dependency may be added.
pitfalls: Half-open by default: a period ending on the 30th needs the 31st as the exclusive end (end.plusDays(1)) or the closed factory - mixing of() and ofClosed() in one codebase duplicates the changeover day.
The factories reject an end before the start but accept an empty range, and an empty range matches nothing while still looking like a valid period.
Converting LocalDate to java.util.Date or to an instant (atStartOfDay(zone).toInstant()) reintroduces the zone; do that only at the persistence or API boundary, never inside the domain object.

variants.name: JDK-only LocalDate pair
variants.implementation_notes: Without ThreeTen-Extra the range is a two-field record: LocalDate from and a nullable LocalDate until, compared with isBefore/isAfter, plus an overlaps() method that respects the null end. Records give value semantics, immutability and a canonical constructor for free, which is most of what the pattern needs. Choose this variant when no dependency may be added or the period must carry domain behaviour the library range does not expose (a precedence rule between intentionally overlapping assignments); ThreeTen-Extra remains the better default because its containment, overlap and abut semantics are already tested and documented.
variants.idiom_name: record with LocalDate from/until (until == null for an open end) + isEffectiveOn/overlaps
pitfalls: A null open end must be handled in every predicate; one missed null check makes the everyday "currently effective" case fail closed.
LocalDate.MIN and LocalDate.MAX as sentinels make duration arithmetic overflow or throw; use null (or an explicit open-end flag) instead.

java.util.Date and Calendar are mutable and carry an instant, not a date - letting either leak into the record destroys the date-only invariant; also never synchronise on a LocalDate, which is a value-based class.
